data.title: Typography
data.tagline: Use text size and style to show what matters first
data.description: Typography separates headings, body text, and supporting information through size, line height, weight, and color. Define a small set of reusable text roles, then adapt them for different screens so readers can find the main point and follow the content.

distinctions.label: Heading
distinctions.explanation: Typography is the full system of text roles and styles, including headings, body copy, and supporting text. A heading is only one text role that marks page or section hierarchy.

use: Create clear levels for page, section, and item headings
Keep long body text comfortable to read
Make dates, notes, and other supporting details quieter
Emphasize a small number of truly important words
avoid: Use so many heading styles that the hierarchy disappears
Set body text too small or too light to read comfortably
Bold a whole paragraph when only one point needs emphasis
Use spaces and line breaks to force alignment; use Space

lessonPractice.title: A settings page gives its heading, descriptions, and permission warning nearly the same size, while the warning is very light gray. What should change?

options.label: Define clear heading, body, and warning roles and keep the warning readable
options.feedback: Each text role has a different job. Consistent size, weight, and contrast reveal the reading order without hiding the warning.

options.label: Bold every piece of text so that every paragraph becomes more prominent
options.feedback: When everything has equal emphasis, headings and warnings lose distinction and the reading order remains unclear.

options.label: Make descriptions and warnings smaller and enlarge only the page title
options.feedback: The title becomes clearer, but required warning text remains difficult to read. Supporting text still needs sufficient legibility.

data.agentPrompt: Refine the settings typography with distinct page heading, section heading, body, and warning roles. Do not make warnings too small or light or bold the entire page. Verify a clear reading order and readable critical text on desktop and mobile.
